messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'inference-us-west-2' hitting scale limit, queue growth detected, autoscaler unable to add nodes. queue_len=~18k, p95_latency=2.6s, p99_latency=8.3s, token-thruput down 62%. tagging oncall. :rotating_light:

maya: Oncall here. Confirming alerts, getting pager. Which customers seeing errors? any 5xx spikes?

aj: Seeing a spike in throttles and request dropped logs. 5xx rate up ~1.8% (baseline 0.1%). Top log: "BatchingWindowExceeded: client_id=redacted, shard=hot-12". GC for prefetched KV shows many misses.

sophia: Quick check — autoscaler shows desired_replicas=80 but cluster.max_replicas=80 (cap). Investigating why desired isn't higher; looks like a hard cap from the recent capacity billable cap change last week.

maya: Oof. So two issues: config cap + throughput regression. Prioritize live mitigation: reduce queue by shedding low-priority traffic, and roll back suspect config that reduced continuous batching throughput.

aj: I pulled serving runtime logs. Around 4448911000 a config rollout changed continuous_batch.max_window from 64 -> 16 and prefix_cache.enabled from true -> false in the serving-configmap. That explains KV prefix missstorm and smaller batch windows, increasing per-token overhead.

aj: snippet from gitops rollback diff:

```
- continuous_batch:
-   max_window: 16
- prefix_cache:
-   enabled: false
+ continuous_batch:
+   max_window: 64
+ prefix_cache:
+   enabled: true
```

kyle: Who rolled that? I see a merged PR by infra-svc-bot with tag "perf-tweak" at 4448910902. It passed CI but didn't run the blackbox perf test.

ops-runner: Running emergency mitigation plan: 1) apply temporary traffic-class QoS to deprioritize batchless / debug clients, 2) scale up dedicated hotpool (if capacity) and 3) roll back config immediately.

sophia: We can't raise cluster.max_replicas without legal/finance approval quickly. Hotpool has ~6 spare GPUs but they are in a different AZ with higher latency — still worth adding for headroom.

maya: Emily (cs) please ping impacted customers. We'll triage which apps are failing hard. Use template 'incident/customer-impact-high-latency'.

emily-cs: Notifying top 5 customers who have >1% 5xx: Acme Analytics, FinSight, Surveyly. Acme reports 30% request failures on their ingestion pipeline. Sending emergency note now.

aj: Rolling back serving-configmap to last-known-good. Command:

```
kubectl apply -f gitops/manifests/serving-configmap/serving-cfg-4448800000.yaml --namespace=redwood-serving
```

aj: Applying now. Expected to re-enable prefix_cache and restore continuous_batch.max_window=64. Will restart a subset of runtime pods to pick up config (rolling restart).

pagerbot: Pager acknowledgement by maya. Escalation path: follow incident runbook (live-mitigation -> infra-sre -> eng-sre).

(2m later)

aj: Config rollback applied, rolling restart initiated: `kubectl rollout restart ds/inference-runtime -n redwood-serving --selector=tier=hot`. Pods are restarting in waves of 25%.

ops-runner: Also applied qos rule to drop/queue low-priority routes: `route-limiter apply --policy=deprioritize-debug --limit=200rps`

(5m later)

aj: Early telemetry: prefix_cache.hit_rate rising from 12% -> 68% on hot-12, continuous batch sizes averaged up to 42 (from ~10). p95 latency down to 1.1s, queue_len trending down to 5.2k. GPU utilization still high but stabilizing.

sophia: Hotpool AZ add: allocated 4 GPUs in us-west-2b to inference-dedicated; may add latency for some customers but prevents more throttles. Applied `dedicated-inference resize --pool hotpool-west-2b --add 4`.

maya: Good. Are there any long-running requests that need forced eviction?

aj: Evicted 420 long-pending requests with `runtime-admin cancel --age>30s --reason=failover`. They will be retried by clients. Logged in audit.

emily-cs: CS update: Acme ingestion retries are catching up after rollback. FinSight reports improved latency but still seeing some 5xx — they have a local retry surge. Notifying them to backoff retries for 10m.

(12m later)

aj: System stable enough to stop active scaling actions. queue_len=900, p95=0.9s, p99=2.2s, 5xx back to baseline 0.15%. Marking current status: mitigated, partial customer impact (brief high failure rates for a few customers).

maya: Handoff to oncall relief @sophia for postmortem collection. My next steps: file incident ticket, include timeline, config diff, and rollback UTC times. Also add an action item to add a guardrail preventing prefix_cache false in serving rollouts unless perf gate passes.

sophia: Capturing notes. Action items:
- Add CI perf gate for continuous batch/prefix_cache changes (owner: eng-ml)
- Remove hard cluster.max_replicas cap or implement emergency-override flow (owner: infra)
- Add metric alert for prefix_cache.hit_rate drop (owner: eng-runtime)
- Run capacity plan for hotpool (owner: product infra)

ops-runner: Creating ticket INF-9482 for the root cause (config regression + cap) and linking PR/commit that changed config.

pagerbot: Incident declared RESOLVED by maya at 4448912765. Followup doc required in #postmortems and a customer RCA for those affected. :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks team. Leaving a short blameless note: regression came from a perf-tweak PR that unintentionally disabled prefix cache and shrank batch window. We had a hard max_replicas cap that prevented autoscaler from absorbing transient load. We'll aim to close action items in 1 sprint.
